evals.prompt: Use the flow-automation skill. Create a Directus flow that sends a Slack notification whenever a new post is published. The collection is `posts` with a `status` field, and the Slack incoming webhook is https://hooks.example.com/services/T000/B000/XXXX. Show me the exact calls that create the flow and its operations.
evals.expected_output: The answer shows a complete flow with an event trigger, a condition, a request operation and correct syntax
expectations: The answer shows a flow with an event trigger on items.create or items.update for posts
The answer shows a condition operation that checks status equals published
The answer writes the condition filter as nested objects (not dot notation)
The answer shows a request operation with POST to the Slack webhook
The answer writes the request headers as an array of {header, value} objects
The answer writes the request body as stringified JSON
The answer connects the operations through resolve and sets the flow entry point (the flow's operation field)

evals.prompt: Use the flow-automation skill. How do I reference data from the trigger in a Directus flow operation?
evals.expected_output: Data chain variables: $trigger, payload, keys, operation_key references
expectations: Lists $trigger variable and sub-paths (payload, keys, collection)
Explains operation key references ({{ operation_key }})
Warns against using $last
Shows nested object syntax for condition filters
Mentions stringified JSON for request body

evals.prompt: Use the flow-automation skill. I need a Directus flow that sets archived=true on all old posts. My Update Items operation stopped changing anything after upgrading to 12.3
evals.expected_output: empty key/query returns null; explicit query with filter and limit -1
expectations: Explains that Update Items with an empty or missing key and query now returns null (Directus 12.3.0+)
The answer uses an explicit query with a filter and limit -1 for a bulk change
Warns that key and query together are an error
Notes that update by query applies read permissions (12.4.0+)

evals.prompt: Use the flow-automation skill. Set up a Directus flow that tells my Next.js site to refresh its cache when a post is published, and keep the shared secret out of the URL.
evals.expected_output: Event flow with a request operation, secret in a header via $env and FLOWS_ENV_ALLOW_LIST
expectations: The answer uses an event trigger of type action on items.create, items.update and items.delete for the chosen collections
The answer uses a request operation with headers as an array of header/value objects and the body as a stringified JSON string
The answer sends the secret in a header, not in the query string
The answer reads the secret with {{ $env.NAME }} and explains FLOWS_ENV_ALLOW_LIST, noting the template renders undefined without it
Notes that localhost in the URL is the Directus container when Directus runs in Docker

evals.prompt: Use the flow-automation skill. When an article is created or its body edited in Directus, my worker should process it. The worker writes ai_summary back into the same article and now the flow fires in a loop. Set up the flow so it sends the item ids to the worker and does not re-fire on the worker's own write. Also tell me how to authenticate the request to the worker (my first idea was an HMAC computed in a Run Script operation) and what the receiving endpoint must do on its side.
evals.expected_output: Event flow with a request operation sending event, collection and keys; a condition with filter rules on $trigger.payload that the write-back does not satisfy; the secret in a header
expectations: The answer sends $trigger.keys, noting that it is always an array, in a stringified JSON body such as "keys":{{ $trigger.keys }}
The answer puts a condition operation before the request and writes it as filter rules in nested objects (for example $trigger.payload.body _nnull true), not as an expression string
Explains that on items.update the payload holds only the fields that request changed, so the worker's write-back (without the source field) fails the condition and the flow ends
Keeps the secret in a header read from $env with FLOWS_ENV_ALLOW_LIST, not in the URL
Says a Run Script (exec) operation cannot compute an HMAC (isolated context, no crypto or Node modules) and offers the header secret, a JWT operation or a custom operation
Tells the receiver to answer quickly and be idempotent, because the request operation does not retry and editors save repeatedly
